headline: Muhurat trading opens Samvat 2083 after the best week since 2021

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning, and a very happy Diwali. It's Sunday, the eighth of November, and this is your Market Brief.

Three things matter most today. First, the stock exchanges open this afternoon for the special Muhurat trading session, the first trade of Samvat 2083. Markets walk into it after their biggest weekly gain since 2021, with the Nifty above 25,000.

Second, Wall Street. An estimated 5.7 trillion dollars was wiped off American shares this week as investors pulled back from AI bets after the Democrats' sweep in Congress. Chip stocks bounced on Friday, but all three major indices still ended the week lower. And some of that money is finding its way to India.

Third, oil. Brent crude was on track for a fall of about 16 percent in a single week, its steepest since the start of the pandemic, on hopes that the war on Iran may ease. For an oil importer like India, that's good news.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Let's start with where markets stand. Indian shares closed the week with the Nifty above 25,000 and the Sensex above 81,000, after their biggest weekly gains since 2021. Economic Times counts a rally of nearly 9 percent in the Sensex over five sessions. Foreign buying, cheaper crude and solid earnings did the lifting.

But there's a catch. Analysts at SAMCO point out that the gains are concentrated in the heavyweights. Many mid caps, small caps and micro caps have actually fallen, which is why your own portfolio may not feel as festive as the index.

Now to the levels. Economic Times sees broader resistance between 25,000 and 25,200 and expects some consolidation. Sudeep Shah of SBI Securities calls 24,750 to 24,800 the key support. He says the bullish view holds as long as the Nifty stays above 24,750, and he suggests some partial profit booking.

On to this afternoon's Muhurat session. The pre-open starts at five past two, and live trade runs from twenty past two for a little over an hour. Business Standard notes that the Sensex and Nifty gained in eight of the ten Muhurat sessions from 2016 to 2025. Treat it as a ceremony, though. It's a thin, short session.

A few big block deals on Friday. SoftBank sold Lenskart shares worth about 1,896 crore rupees at 697 rupees apiece, all picked up by thirteen institutions. Peak XV Partners and YC Holdings sold Groww shares worth 2,457 crore rupees, and Groww fell almost 4 percent to 215 rupees. V2 Retail's promoters sold shares worth 258 crore rupees, yet the stock rose seven and a half percent.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
Now to the IPO pipeline, and a big name has joined it. Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings, the parent of Coca-Cola's Indian bottling business, has filed its draft papers with Sebi. The issue is entirely an offer for sale of nearly 100 crore shares by its promoter, which Mint says is up to 15 percent of the company. So none of the money goes to the company itself. It reported revenue of 11,663 crore rupees last financial year, and Moneycontrol says the listing is planned for 2027.

Also filing this week is IL Jin Electronics, a subsidiary of Amber Enterprises. It wants to raise 2,500 crore rupees, all through fresh shares. Most of the money will go to repaying debt and buying plant and machinery.

Encube Ethicals, backed by Quadria Capital, has Sebi's approval for a 3,000 crore rupee IPO. The promoter will sell up to 2,000 crore rupees of shares, and the Quadria-managed investor up to 1,000 crore.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
On to results, starting with auto parts. Samvardhana Motherson's September-quarter profit rose 42 percent to about 1,175 crore rupees, on revenue up nearly 27 percent. Uno Minda's profit grew about 37 percent to 441 crore rupees, with revenue up 38 percent.

In energy, ONGC's quarterly profit jumped 57 percent from a year ago, and the company says it could win operating rights at two Venezuelan oil projects in the coming months. Nuvama, though, kept its Reduce rating, pointing to production that keeps declining.

Bayer CropScience grew its profit to 166 crore rupees from 153 crore, and declared an interim dividend of 90 rupees a share. The record date is the twelfth of November.

And one stock to watch tomorrow. Tata Power has lost a legal battle with Kleros Capital in a Singapore court, in a case worth about 650 million dollars. Experts quoted by Mint believe it could wipe out the company's entire profit for the year.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
Now to tax, and the debate over capital gains is getting louder ahead of next year's Budget. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman says she will consider investors' concerns on equity taxation. She noted that foreign money has started to come back, but that changed circumstances have amplified calls for a friendlier tax regime.

The proposals are piling up. The industry body FICCI wants the long-term capital gains tax on listed shares removed, with a higher securities transaction tax on delivery trades to make up the revenue. SBI Research has suggested a 2 lakh rupee exemption and no tax at all after three years, paired with a 50 percent rise in the transaction tax. It puts the cost at 40,000 to 50,000 crore rupees and says the government can absorb it. And Edelweiss chairman Rashesh Shah wants capital gains tax scrapped for foreign portfolio investors, to revive inflows and support the rupee.

On the rupee itself, Sebi has cut the limit for unhedged currency derivative positions from 100 million dollars to just 5 million. The aim is to curb speculation on a falling rupee while leaving genuine hedgers alone.

On the farm front, a worrying number. Rabi sowing is down 46 percent from last year. Only 37.6 lakh hectares had been sown by the end of October, against 69 lakh a year ago, with October rainfall 48 percent below normal. Oilseeds and pulses are the worst hit.

One more. The GST Council has proposed ending arrest powers under section 69 of the GST law. Prosecution and penalties would stay, but Parliament still has to pass the change.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Around the world, it was a brutal week on Wall Street. Worries about sky-high valuations, rising debt and uncertain returns on AI spending came to a head, and the Democrats' sweep of Congress added fears of curbs on the data centres driving the boom. On Thursday, the Nasdaq 100 had its worst single day since the pandemic, and the S&P 500 posted its biggest weekly drop since 2025.

Friday brought a bounce. Chip stocks led, with the Philadelphia semiconductor index up 4.2 percent, helped by a strong October jobs report. The S&P 500 rose a third of a percent to 7,377, and the Nasdaq gained about 1 percent. The Dow slipped about half a percent. The Nasdaq has now fallen four weeks in a row. Next week, investors will watch American inflation data and more tech earnings.

What does this mean for us? Mint reports that the unwinding of the AI trade is reviving demand for out-of-favour Indian and Chinese shares. Asia's chip exporters may suffer if American AI spending slows, but falling oil helps importers like India.

On oil, Brent was headed for a weekly fall of about 16 percent, on hopes of de-escalation in the US-Israeli war on Iran, even as tanker attacks continue.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Finally, your money, and a timely one on Diwali gifts. Gifts from friends are tax-free only up to 50,000 rupees in a year. CA Swati Jain explains that if the total crosses that limit, the entire amount becomes taxable, not just the excess. Gifts from relatives remain exempt.

Three tribunal rulings worth knowing. The income tax appellate tribunal in Surat deleted a capital gains addition of 2.45 crore rupees on a land sale. Form 26AS showed 2.86 crore rupees, but the landowner proved he had received only 25 lakh rupees in that year, with the rest coming in instalments. In Jaipur, the tribunal accepted a 24 lakh rupee gift from a grandmother as genuine, on the strength of land records and an affidavit. And in another Surat case, a retired employee won his leave encashment exemption of about 8 lakh rupees, because the tax department hadn't followed due process before changing a processed return.

On gold, prices are about 21 percent below their domestic record high. Gold exchange traded fund folios have grown 164 percent in three years, and one study warns against buying out of fear of missing out, suggesting gold stay at 5 to 10 percent of a portfolio. If you're exchanging old jewellery this Diwali, check purity, net weight and melting deductions before accepting the jeweller's valuation.

And an investor warning. Bengaluru police have begun a probe into the Stockal case. Its parent company says thirteen investors lost 6.26 million dollars, about 59 crore rupees.

So what to watch today? The Muhurat session from twenty past two this afternoon, with the Nifty's 24,750 support and 25,200 resistance in view. Tomorrow, watch Tata Power after its Singapore court setback, and then American inflation data later in the week. Remember, markets are shut on Tuesday for Balipratipada. Wishing you and your family a bright and prosperous Diwali. That's your Market Brief.
